identity.title: Scaling Atomistic Protein Binder Design with Generative Pretraining and Test-Time Compute

problem.claim: Atomistic de novo protein binder design must generate binders against target structures while supporting broader design objectives.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a false dichotomy between conditional generation and sequence optimization through structure predictors, motivating a unified approach.

contributions.claim: Proteina-Complexa, a fully atomistic binder-generation method that unifies generative modeling with hallucination-style sequence optimization.
Teddymer, a large-scale synthetic binder-target dataset constructed from domain-domain interactions in monomeric predicted structures for pretraining.
Inference-time optimization strategies built on a generative prior, extending the unified design framework to interface, fold-class, small-molecule, and enzyme-design objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that Proteina-Complexa is novel in fully atomistically unifying previously presented generative and hallucination paradigms, alongside new Teddymer data and test-time optimization strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report markedly higher in-silico success rates than existing generative approaches on computational binder-design benchmarks.
The authors report that their test-time optimization strategies greatly outperform previous hallucination methods under normalized compute budgets.
The authors report surpassing prior methods on interface hydrogen-bond optimization, fold-class-guided generation, and extensions to small-molecule targets and enzyme-design tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract positions structure-based de novo binder design as conditional generation or hallucination-style sequence optimization.
It challenges that separation and introduces the fully atomistic Proteina-Complexa framework.
It extends flow-based latent generation architectures, creates Teddymer from predicted-structure interactions, and combines it with experimental multimers to train a base model.
It applies inference-time optimization and reports benchmark gains, broader design demonstrations, and public release plans.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a conceptual unification of two design paradigms to a concrete generative prior, a pretraining dataset, and test-time optimization.

lessons.interpretation: A strong paper narrative can make a framing claim actionable by mapping it to distinct system components and evaluation settings.
lessons.application: When arguing that two approaches are not truly separate, define the shared mechanism, identify the data or model component that connects them, and evaluate both the unified system and paradigm-specific baselines.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the approaches address genuinely different objectives or cannot share representations without obscuring important constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide benchmark names, numerical success rates, sample sizes, statistical uncertainty, or details of the normalized compute budgets.
It does not specify the experimental multimer data, training procedure, or whether the reported extensions were evaluated under comparable conditions.
The promised public release is stated, but availability and exact contents are not established here.
